Scottish Islands Motorcycle Guide

Scotland's islands offer some of the most dramatic and remote motorcycle touring in Europe. Here are six essential island destinations with ferry details.

  1. Isle of Skye — No ferry needed (bridge). Trotternish Loop. 1–2 days.
  2. Isle of Mull — Ferry: Oban–Craignure (45 min). Quiet single-track paradise. 1–2 days.
  3. Isle of Arran — Ferry: Ardrossan–Brodick (55 min). Scotland in miniature. 1 day.
  4. Outer Hebrides — Ferry: Ullapool–Stornoway or Uig–Tarbert. Epic island chain. 3–5 days.
  5. Orkney — Ferry: Scrabster–Stromness (90 min). Viking history, wild cliffs. 2–3 days.
  6. Isle of Bute — Ferry: Wemyss Bay–Rothesay (35 min). Easy day trip from Glasgow.

Total island riding: 1000+ miles possible. Book ferries via CalMac and NorthLink. Read our NC500: Scotland's Ultimate Motorcycle Route Map guide for more. keyTakeaways: Six Scottish islands offer some of Europe's most dramatic and remote motorcycle touring.
Skye needs no ferry thanks to its bridge, with the Trotternish Loop the highlight.
The Outer Hebrides form an epic island chain best explored over three to five days.
Ferry times range from a 35-minute Bute hop to a 90-minute Orkney crossing.
Book ferries in advance via CalMac and NorthLink, especially in peak season.

faq.q: Do I need a ferry to reach the Isle of Skye?
faq.a: No. The Skye Bridge connects the island to the mainland, so you can ride straight across without booking a ferry. This makes Skye one of the easiest Scottish islands to include in a tour. The Trotternish Loop in the north is the riding highlight, taking in the Old Man of Storr and dramatic coastal scenery.

faq.q: How do I book ferries to the Scottish islands?
faq.a: Most west coast island ferries are run by CalMac, while NorthLink serves Orkney and Shetland. Book online in advance, especially for popular crossings in summer, as motorcycle spaces can fill up. Arrive early at the terminal, and note that some smaller crossings operate reduced timetables outside the main season.

faq.q: Which Scottish island is best for a short trip?
faq.a: The Isle of Bute is ideal for a day trip, with a quick 35-minute ferry from Wemyss Bay, easily reached from Glasgow. Arran, sometimes called Scotland in miniature, packs varied scenery into a single day. Both offer a taste of island riding without committing to a multi-day expedition.

faq.q: How many days do I need for the Outer Hebrides?
faq.a: Allow three to five days to do the Outer Hebrides justice. The chain of islands, linked by causeways and short ferries, stretches a long way, and the roads are single-track in places. Rushing means missing the beaches, machair and remote atmosphere that make the Hebrides special. Book accommodation ahead, as options are limited.

faq.q: What should I know about riding on the islands?
faq.a: Expect single-track roads with passing places, so learn the etiquette of pulling in and letting faster or oncoming traffic through. Fuel and services are sparse, so fill up when you can. Weather changes quickly, sheep roam freely, and daylight is long in summer but short in the shoulder seasons, so plan your days accordingly.
